subject: MAP: Technical evaluation slate — latency & cost goals
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harper <tom.harper@healthgrid.com>, Priya Shah <priya@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation slate — latency & cost goals

Tom / Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and an initial MAP milestone for the technical evaluation so we can align scope and owners. I attached a one‑page MAP workbook (HG_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a simple latency/cost CSV you can run against your baseline harness (latency-benchmark-template.csv).

Highlights from the call (technical):
- Primary success criteria: parity with current unoptimized baseline on quality and meeting operational SLOs for latency and cost during peak traffic.
- Latency targets (preliminary): p50 <= 120 ms, p95 <= 450 ms for 512 token inference window (batching allowed; tail latency matters).
- Unit cost target: goal <= $0.05 per 1k generated tokens at scale (workload: mixed short prompts + 2–3 passives per session).
- Model shortlist for initial eval: Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8), Llama2-13B (4-bit quant), Open-Chat-Redwood-Shared-13B (optimised kernels). We should validate both quality and cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Constraints: Health data will be de-identified for eval runs; final private deployment may require VPC + customer KMS.

Proposed MAP milestone (technical eval):
- Deliverable: benchmark report with throughput/latency/cost table + sample outputs for 3 eval prompts
- Owner (Redwood): Connor O'Brien — run benchmarks, supply harness and results
- Owner (HealthGrid): Tom Harper / Priya Shah — provide representative prompt set, sample traffic profile, infra access (VPN/credentials for private runs)
- Target completion: 2026-09-24 (two-week sprint)
- Dependencies: access to HealthGrid test environment, baseline harness run, SOC2 evidence request if we need private infra access

Next steps: please confirm owners & target completion or suggest a date that matches your infra availability. I can circulate an updated MAP workbook with milestones once we lock the date.

Attachments: HG_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP draft), latency-benchmark-template.csv (CSV to feed to benchmark harness)

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0143
https://redwood.ai

From: Tom Harper <tom.harper@healthgrid.com>

Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation slate — latency & cost goals

Thanks Tessa — that summary is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 
- We can provide an initial prompt set and traffic profile by EOD Friday (09/11).
- Important constraint: if any test runs touch PHI-like data, those runs must be isolated in our private VPC. For the first pass please stick to de-identified test data.
- Add metric: memory footprint (GPU memory at steady state) and token-efficiency (prompt+response tokens per successful transaction) to the benchmark table.

I've attached our infra spec (HGrid-infra-specs.pdf) which lists available GPU classes and network topology. If Redwood needs specific drivers/containers we can provision a small test node.

Agree with the 9/24 target if we can kick off by 9/13. I'll confirm availability for the week of 9/13 tomorrow.

Tom
VP Product Engineering | HealthGrid
Tom.harper@healthgrid.com
Attachment: HGrid-infra-specs.pdf

Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation slate — latency & cost goals

Great — thank you Tom. We will: 
- Add memory footprint and token-efficiency columns to the benchmark template.
- Keep all initial runs on de-identified data; for any VPC/private runs we'll coordinate an SOC2 checklist ahead of time.

Connor, Marissa — I updated the MAP workbook with Tom's infra notes and added a row for "memory footprint" in the benchmark sheet. Can you review the updated workbook and confirm the run plan (tags: "smoke", "scale", "tail")? I'm aiming to lock the kickoff on Mon 2026-09-13.

Tom/Priya — if 9/13 works we plan to: 
- 9/13: tech kickoff (30m) to sync on harness, credentials, prompt set
- 9/14–9/20: benchmark runs (smoke then scale)
- 9/21–9/23: SLO & quality review, produce report
- 9/24: MAP milestone complete, deliver benchmark report and recommended model variant

I attached the updated MAP workbook as HG_MAP_v1.xlsx (version 2 has change log).

Thanks,
Tessa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation slate — latency & cost goals

Looping in a few technical comments for the benchmark plan (quick bullets):
- Benchmark harness: use fixed seed prompts and 1000-sample sample set across short/medium/long prompts (prompt lengths: 32/128/512). Capture p50/p95/p99 for each bucket.
- Latency targets (suggested acceptance): p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 450ms, p99 <= 900ms for the 128-token window using batching up to 8 where applicable. These are slightly relaxed from the sales target to ensure realistic acceptance while we optimize kernels.
- Cost accounting: measure GPU time + instance amortized cost + memory IO. Report cost per 1k generated tokens and include token-efficiency delta vs baseline. Acceptance: <= $0.06 per 1k generated tokens (initial).
- Model shortlist addendum: include an additional smaller candidate for throughput tests — Red-OpenLite-6B (quantized).
- Failure modes: include checks for OOM, excessive context eviction, and prompt token drop-offs; capture logs and KV cache stats.

Connor — can you prepare a simple runbook (one-pager) we can hand to HealthGrid that lists container image, driver version, benchmark command, and expected outputs? If we want to run in their VPC we will need their ephemeral credentials noted in the MAP workbook.

I can help with the harness and will own the acceptance criteria table in the report.

-rishi
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference

Let's lock 9/13 at 10:00 AM PT for the kickoff. I'll send a calendar invite and include the contact for our infra engineer (cc'd Priya).

Tom
